properties.decision:
DECIDED 2026-08-25 by Anthony, in one line: *"make the ladder open."* Asked as a straight fork — add `assembly` as a sixth enum value, or make the ladder user-defined — and he took the second.

═══ WHAT IS BEING REPLACED ═══

`schema/structure.yaml:18` declares `Component.level` as a CLOSED enum: `[component, subsystem, system, system_of_systems, enterprise]`, default `component`. `crates/reflow2-core/src/hierarchy.rs` mirrors it as `enum Level` with `as_str`, `from_key` and `rank()` (component = 0 … enterprise = 4). `hierarchy_issues` compares the ranks either side of a `CONTAINS` and reports `level_mismatch` when a parent is not exactly one rung above its child.

⇒ **`component` IS A HARD FLOOR.** There is no value to give a part of a component, so that containment cannot be expressed at all. Measured 2026-08-25 by hitting it — `fact:the-level-ladder-has-a-hard-floor-at-component-and-no-assembly-rung`, which is the EVIDENCE; this node is the DECISION taken because of it.

═══ WHY OPEN AND NOT ONE MORE RUNG ═══

Anthony's research gives the canonical four-tier hierarchy — System / Subsystem / **Assembly** / Component — and reflow2 is missing the third. Adding `assembly` would have fixed the case that exposed this and cost almost nothing.

⭐⭐ IT WAS DECLINED BECAUSE OF THE STRONGER POINT IN HIS OWN RESEARCH: **"atomic" SHIFTS BY DOMAIN.** In his table the atomic unit is a microprocessor chip for aerospace and a single code module for software. A ladder with fixed named rungs asserts that every domain bottoms out at the same conceptual depth, and his examples show they do not. One more enum value would move the floor down one and leave the assertion in place.

It also matches ORIGINAL intent rather than adding to it. `req:recursive-black-box-decomposition` (accepted, his words, 2026-08-07) already says *"this continues down further and further as the design needs... from code projects to biology projects."* The closed enum is what makes the downward half of that unsatisfiable.

═══ WHAT THIS MUST NOT INHERIT ═══

🛑 THE LADDER IS DECLARED TWICE AND NOTHING CHECKS THEY AGREE — `schema/structure.yaml` and `hierarchy.rs::Level`. `from_key` maps any unrecognised string to `Component`, so a rung added to the YAML and forgotten in Rust silently ranks 0 and every containment involving it reads as a mismatch. **A silent fallback, in a project holding `req:no-silent-fallback` at critical priority**, and the same two-places-one-truth shape the absorption found in `#[non_exhaustive]` match arms. An open ladder makes this worse if carried forward, because the rungs stop being a compile-time set at all: the ordering has to become DATA with exactly one home.

═══ WHAT IS NOT SETTLED, AND MUST NOT BE ASSUMED ═══

The decision is that the ladder is open. HOW is not decided, and these are the real questions:
- **Where do the rungs live?** Per-design nodes, a property on the Project, or a document — and what happens to a design that never declares any.
- **Do the five current names survive as a default ladder?** 93 components carry them today; whatever ships must not invalidate them or force a migration on anyone.
- **Does `hierarchy_issues` still demand exactly-one-rung steps?** With user-defined rungs, "one level at a time" is a claim about the user's ladder, not about a universal one.
- **What replaces `rank()`** now that ordering is data rather than a match arm.
- **What else keys on the enum** — `scan_nodes(level=…)`, `move_component`, the level-spine-disagreement detector, the granularity guidance.

📌 THE STOPPING RULES ARE REFERENCE, NOT MECHANISM. Anthony's four rules for how deep to go — procurement black box, LRU/maintenance, single discipline or owner, verification cost — are recorded on the evidence fact. Nothing in reflow2 says how deep is deep enough, and an open ladder makes that question sharper rather than answering it. Rule 1 lands on a known gap: nothing distinguishes a component that was BOUGHT from one that was BUILT.

⚠️ NOTHING WAS IMPLEMENTED. Decided at the end of a long session, immediately before Anthony went to bed. No code, no schema change, no branch.

KEPT DISTINCT from `fact:the-level-ladder-has-a-hard-floor-at-component-and-no-assembly-rung` after reading it: that is a dated MEASUREMENT of the floor and carries the research and the stopping rules. This is the CHOICE made in response, with the road not taken and its reasoning. Folding a decision into an observation would lose which one is evidence and which one is a commitment.
properties.name: DECIDED — the decomposition ladder becomes OPEN: a design defines its own rungs, as many as it needs, instead of choosing from five fixed names
properties.rationale:
Recorded as its own accepted Decision rather than as a note on the requirement, because it is a CHOICE between two named options that was actually made, and the road not taken has reasoning worth keeping: adding `assembly` was cheaper, sufficient for the case that exposed the problem, and rejected on the domain-shifting-atomicity argument rather than on cost.

ACCEPTED rather than proposed because Anthony gave it as an instruction in his own words, not as a musing.
